Saving Our Planet 1: Climate Change

May 20, 2024

Key Words: “Environment” “Persuasive “

Vocabularies: century , atmosphere , renewable , deforestation , generations , carbon dioxide , temperature

Joe original version

Did you know that the Earth’s temperature has been increasing for over a century? That is a crisis, a challenge of planet-saving. In this essay, I will explain the causes of climate change, its effects, and what we can do to help.

One of the main causes of climate change is burning fossil, like coal, oil and gas; cars and factories all burn fossil fuels, releasing carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere, making the planet warmer.

Climate change affects the Earth in many ways. For example, the heat of the rising temperature melts ice from the Arctic and Antarctica, making the planet warmer; Penguins, polar bears, and seals will lose their habitat and diet, and the rising sea level will cause floods.

Despite the terrible effects of climate crisis, there are also many solutions to solve this problem. Little by little. We can start by using renewable energy like solar power instead of burning fossil fuels, plant more trees to stop deforestation, and many other ways together we can stop climate change starting with communities, then countries, and eventually the whole world.

Climate change is caused by burning fossil fuels, it caused the ice to melt which leads to flowers, but we can stop it by using renewable energy and planting more trees. It is important for all of us to work together and protect the planet for future generations.

Dad revised version

Did you know Earth’s temperature has increased for over a century? Research from NASA indicates that the average Earth’s surface temperature has risen 1.8 degrees over the past 30 years. People call this “climate crisis” a challenge of planet-saving. In this essay, I will explain the major causes of climate change and how it affects human life, then explore the possible solutions and approaches to improve such a problem to restore and bring sustainability for future generations.

Human activities such as “burning fossil fuels,” “deforestation,” and “industrialization” can be the main causes of climate change.

Coal, oil, and gas have become the most important energy sources supporting transportation and construction in the past few decades. Every day, cars and factories consume fossil fuels, releasing carbon dioxide that traps heat in the atmosphere, making the planet warmer globally.

Moreover, heat increases temperature levels, which impacts all living things in ecosystems; recent research shows that the ice in the Arctic and Antarctica has reduced significantly compared to 200 years ago, and rising sea levels bring significant threats to all coastal cities with potential floods.

Wild animals such as penguins, polar bears, and seals and their habitat and diet have been permanently changed/impacted. Scientists forecast that some species living in the North Pole will be distinct in a few years. Fishes and coral reefs under the sea are also facing challenges in finding a suitable environment in which to live.

In addition, all modern civilization heavily relies on oil and coal; sustainable solutions are necessary for future generations living on this beautiful planet to avoid limited resources and a terrible environment.

Despite the urgent situation and challenges of our planet/environment, many countries, scientists, and universities continuously invent and apply possible new energy solutions. For examples, Japan recently published policies to force half of the new car registrations to only electric vehicles. The Australian government rewards new homes that install solar power as renewable energy. China has planted 1 million trees in the northern region in the past ten years to stop deforestation. With the efforts of each country, community, and individual, people are constantly making a difference in stopping climate change.

In conclusion, climate change has been a major issue for centuries, and it will be a disaster if no action is taken worldwide; it is time to work together and protect the planet for future generations.

ChatGPT revised version

  • Climate Change: Causes, Effects, and Solutions

Did you know that Earth’s temperature has been rising for over a century? Research from NASA indicates that the average surface temperature of the Earth has risen by 1.8 degrees over the past 30 years. People refer to this as a “climate crisis,” which poses a significant challenge for saving our planet. In this essay, I will explain the major causes of climate change, how it affects human life, and explore possible solutions to restore sustainability for future generations.

  • Causes of Climate Change

Human activities such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrialization are the main causes of climate change. Coal, oil, and gas have been the primary energy sources supporting transportation and construction for the past few decades. Every day, cars and factories consume fossil fuels, releasing carbon dioxide (CO2) that traps heat in the atmosphere, causing the planet to warm globally. Deforestation, the cutting down of trees, also contributes to climate change. Trees absorb CO2, and when they are removed, more CO2 remains in the atmosphere, worsening the greenhouse effect. Industrial processes, such as manufacturing cement and steel, release additional greenhouse gases, further warming the planet.

  • Effects of Climate Change

The increase in global temperatures impacts all living things in ecosystems. Recent research shows that ice in the Arctic and Antarctica has significantly melted compared to 200 years ago. Rising sea levels significantly threaten coastal cities, potentially causing devastating floods. Wild animals such as penguins, polar bears, and seals are seeing their habitats and food sources permanently altered. Scientists predict that some species living in the North Pole may become extinct in a few years. Marine life, including fish and coral reefs, also faces challenges in finding suitable environments due to changing ocean temperatures and acidity.

  • Solutions to Climate Change

Modern civilization heavily relies on oil and coal, so sustainable solutions are necessary to ensure future generations can live on this beautiful planet without depleting resources or damaging the environment. Despite the urgent situation, many countries, scientists, and universities are continuously developing and applying new energy solutions. For example, Japan recently implemented policies requiring half of all new car registrations to be electric vehicles. The Australian government offers rewards for new homes that install solar panels as a renewable energy source. In China, over the past ten years, 1 million trees have been planted in the northern region to combat deforestation. With the combined efforts of each country, community, and individual, people are making a difference in addressing climate change.

  • Conclusion

In conclusion, climate change has been a major issue for centuries, and it will become a disaster if no action is taken worldwide. It is time for us all to work together to protect the planet for future generations.
